result.title: The APL Doesn't Fall Far From The Tree: Unsupervised Artefact Prototype Learning in Histopathology
result.summary: Histopathology foundation models provide rich representations of tissue morphology, but technical artefacts in whole slide images introduce noise that may impact diagnostic accuracy. We introduce Artefact Prototype Learning (APL), a novel approach to detecting these artefacts that exploits the geometry of pre-trained embedding spaces without manual labels or fine-tuning. Rather than treating artefacts as isolated outliers, APL computes prototypes of out-of-distribution patches and uses them to distinguish artefact-associated patterns from tissue. Evaluation on a single-centre dataset shows that APL outperforms prior methods GrandQC and HistoART in detecting artefacts such as blur, dark spots, slide edges and pen marks, but struggles with tissue folds and blood. These results show that frozen pre-trained embeddings already carry information that allows artefact detection without expensive labels or vast computational resources.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 APL，在冻结的病理基础模型嵌入空间中用 out-of-distribution patch 原型无监督地区分技术伪影与组织，无需标签或微调，单中心数据上优于 GrandQC 与 HistoART，但组织褶皱和血液识别较弱。
AI.relevance_reason: 其利用预训练嵌入几何做原型式 OOD 判别，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选与无效 patch 剔除提供线索，但属医学影像应用，与 latent 推理状态生成无直接关系，需较多核查。
